ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic perianal disease with recent worsening of symptoms and development of mucinous discharge, pain, and perianal induration
salient_findings: Internal fistula opening at the dentate line
key_facts: History of incision and drainage of a recurrent perianal abscess
Two indurated, ulcerative lesions around the anus
Internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line
Normal mucosa in the rectum and colon
Abdominopelvic CT and MRI showed a well-defined mass
No inguinal nodal or distant metastases
Serum carcinoembryonic antigen level within normal range

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: 12-year history of perianal fistula and recent worsening of symptoms

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcerative lesions and fistula openings around the anus

shortlist.label: Adenocarcinoma of the rectum
shortlist.why_kept: Internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line

shortlist.label: Anorectal melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcerative lesions and mass at the anorectal junction

shortlist.label: Perianal fistula with secondary infection
shortlist.why_kept: History of perianal fistula and recent onset of mucinous discharge

shortlist.label: Anal intraepithelial neoplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormalities around the anus and potential for malignant transformation

shortlist.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic perianal disease with ulcerative lesions

raw.rationale: Histological examination of a biopsy specimen from the indurated area revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, which directly explains the mucinous discharge, pain, and perianal induration, and is consistent with the imaging findings of a well-defined mass at the anorectal junction.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: While Crohn's disease can cause perianal fistulas and mucinous discharge, the histological examination revealing mucinous adenocarcinoma does not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus
rejected.why: The histological examination specifically identified mucinous adenocarcinoma, not squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the rectum
rejected.why: The mass is described at the level of the anorectal junction extending into the right ischiorectal fossa, and the internal fistula opening is at the right side of the dentate line, which is more consistent with an anal primary than a rectal primary.

rejected.label: Anorectal melanoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of melanoma in the histological examination, which instead revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Perianal fistula with secondary infection
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of perianal fistula, the presence of mucinous adenocarcinoma explains the current symptoms and findings more comprehensively than a simple fistula with infection.

rejected.label: Anal intraepithelial neoplasia
rejected.why: This condition is a precursor to invasive cancer but does not explain the invasive features and symptoms presented by the patient.

rejected.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
rejected.why: This condition can cause perianal lesions and fistulas but does not account for the mucinous adenocarcinoma found on histological examination.
